Currently the google-workspace MCP exposes ~80+ tools (Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar, Chat, Tasks, Forms, Slides, Contacts, Apps Script, Custom Search). Most users only need 4-5 tools. Loading all 80 adds 33% token cost per turn vs 7% in Claude Code which lazy-loads tools.
Supporting per-MCP tool allowlisting would let users load only the specific tools they need, cutting MCP schema cost significantly even before deferred loading is implemented.
For reference: I have 7 MCPs connected and ~65% of that 33% cost comes from google-workspace alone. Loading just gmail + drive + docs + calendar would cut it roughly in half.

Want to take this. Deterministic repro across providers; PR shortly.

**Repro:** parallel `opencode run` against ~10 models, same prompt. 8 return in 36s–7min; `mimo/mimo-v2.5-pro` and `minimax/MiniMax-M2.7` spawn the Explore Agent subagent and never return. Pre-inlining the files referenced in the prompt (so the model has no reason to invoke Explore Agent) makes both complete in <5min. The hang is on the subagent → parent return path, not the model.

This matches the broader pattern across #24669, #23296, #13841, #21250, #22252, #18378, #23891 — all converge on the same root: `tool/task.ts` awaits `ops.prompt(...)` with no timeout, so any stall in the subagent path hangs the parent indefinitely.

**Approach** (mirroring `bash.ts`):
- Optional `timeout: number` (ms) on the Task Parameters schema.
- `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_TASK_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` flag, default ~10 min.
- Race `ops.prompt(...)` against `Effect.sleep(timeout)`. On timeout: `ops.cancel(nextSession.id)` and return a `<task_error>` block with the `task_id` so the caller can retry with a larger timeout, narrow the scope, or fall back.

Please assign if no objections.

Hi @Br1an67 — I filed #24871 yesterday for #3523 and missed that this PR was already open with green checks. Apologies for the duplication; you got there first.

Your fix is the right shape. One small follow-up note (not a blocker for this PR) for whenever a maintainer reviews:

`name.slice(0, 64)` will collide if two `<server>_<tool>` strings share the first 64 chars after concat. Two distinct tools end up writing to the same `result[name]` key, and the second silently overwrites the first. Edge case — it requires the same MCP server with two long tool names sharing a 55+ char prefix (since `_` adds one and the server name eats the rest). But because the value is silently dropped instead of erroring, it's the same shape as the original bug (silent failure, no signal to the user).

A content-derived suffix preserves uniqueness:

```ts
if (name.length > 64) {
  const hash = Hash.fast(name).slice(0, 8)
  name = name.slice(0, 64 - hash.length - 1) + "_" + hash
}
```

Posted this here rather than as a competing PR. If the maintainer prefers the truncate-only path you have, that's a fine call — collisions are rare and the warning log surfaces them. Closing #24871. Happy to PR the suffix as a follow-up after this lands if it's wanted.

Closing — #15595 by @Br1an67 was opened 2026-03-01 with passing checks and addresses the same issue. I missed it during prior-art review and shouldn't have filed a competing PR. Apologies for the noise.

The collision-safety refinement (hash suffix vs blind slice) is now a follow-up suggestion on #15595: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/15595#issuecomment-4355397466

If maintainers prefer this implementation over #15595 for any reason I haven't anticipated, happy to reopen — but the right path forward is to land #15595 first.
